summary:
Allwork.Space reports on AI adoption data (attributed to a new WeWork report) showing U.S. business AI use rose from 17.7% in January to 21.7% in July 2026, but unevenly. Expectations have cooled: in January firms expected a 4.7 percentage point increase over six months; by July that expectation fell to 2.8 points.

Company size is the sharpest divide. Only 20.8% of businesses with one to four employees used AI in July, versus 38.8% of those with 250 or more employees. In the Information sector, firms with 250+ employees hit 77% adoption, the highest in the data. By office-based industry: Information 43.7%, Professional, Scientific & Technical Services 37.6%, Finance & Insurance 36%, Real Estate 29%, Health Care 24.7%.

Geography also varies. Fifteen of the 25 largest metros exceeded the 21.7% national rate. Tampa rose 14.9 points to 32%; Detroit rose 11.4 points to 24.5%. Phoenix, January's leader at 30.1%, fell 8.6 points to 21.5%. Baltimore, Houston, Portland and San Diego also declined. New York (17.9%) and Los Angeles (19.7%) sat below the national average.

Use cases skew toward assisting employees: 85.4% use generative AI for writing and editing documents, emails and communications; 49.9% for information searches; 44.6% for summarizing or analyzing documents. By function, sales and marketing led at 14.3%, strategy and business development 12.4%, R&D 11.2%.

Employment effects appear minimal: 95.7% of AI-using businesses reported no change in total employment, 2% a decrease, 2.3% an increase. AI supplemented or enhanced a task at 43.7% of firms; 10.1% said it performed work previously done by a worker.

Among non-adopters, 61.6% said AI is not applicable to their business, 22% cited limited understanding, 20.7% cited privacy and security concerns. Among one-to-four-employee firms, 63.3% cited non-applicability.
